brief: August's rally was earnings-driven: Q2 S&P 500 profits rose 31.1% year-over-year (strongest since 2021), keeping the index at an unchanged 20X forward P/E despite a 12% YTD gain, so earnings, not valuation expansion, explain the move. A shock July payrolls loss of 23,000 (prior months revised down 103,000) pushed labor-force participation to a 5.5-year low, cutting September hike odds to 44% from 57% and rallying stocks on bad-news-is-good-news logic. But PCE inflation held at 3.7% and retail sales fell, setting up a growth-versus-inflation standoff the market could not resolve in one direction. Long-end yields hit multi-decade highs (30-year 5.327%, 10-year 4.739%) until the Treasury doubled bond buybacks, only for Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech to push September hike odds back above 60% and end the easing narrative. Nvidia beat estimates and guided fiscal 2028 revenue growth near 70%, yet still fell after Warsh spoke. Oil finished flat despite renewed Hormuz strikes, as weak Chinese demand offset the geopolitical premium, while refined-product prices hit post-2022 highs. Gold, silver and Bitcoin led as a 'debasement trade'; Warsh's hawkishness cut the rally short-term, and the piece calls the trade structurally bullish but tactically fragile.
